motions.motion_text: Councilmember Toor moved, seconded by McGrath to adopt Ordinance No. 7403 which adopts a budget for the City of Boulder, Colorado, for the fiscal year commencing on the first day of January, 2005 and ending on the last day of December, 2005, and setting forth details in relation thereto.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:2; Riggle and Stoakes opposed, Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Riggle moved, seconded by Stoakes to introduce an ordinance to rescind the Trash Tax component from the 2005 Budget.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 3:5; Bohannan, Gray, McGrath, Ruzzin and Toor opposed; Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Gray moved, seconded by McGrath to adopt Ordinance No. 7404 which establishes the 2004 City of Boulder property tax mill levies which are to be collected by the County of Boulder, State of Colorado, within the City of Boulder in 2005 for payment of expenditures by the City of Boulder, County of Boulder, State of Colorado, and setting forth details in relation thereto.

Councilmember Stoakes moved, seconded by Eldridge to adopt Ordinance No. 7405 which appropriates money to defray expenses and liabilities of the City of Boulder, Colorado, for the 2005 fiscal year of the City of Boulder, commencing on the first day of January 2005, and ending on the last day of December 2005, and setting forth details in relation thereto.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:1; Riggle opposed, Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Eldridge moved, seconded by Gray to adopt Ordinance No. 7406 which amends Chapters 3-8, 3-9, 3-10, 3-11 and 4-20, B.R.C. 1981, changing certain fees and setting forth details in relation thereto.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:2; Riggle and Stoakes opposed; Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Gray moved, seconded by Stoakes to direct the City Manager to bring back funding options to restore $15,000 to the library when the city has a clear idea of the revenue picture for 2004.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:2; Eldridge and Riggle opposed; Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Stoakes offered a friendly amendment to cut council meals as one option.
motions.vote_text: The friendly amendment was not accepted.

motions.motion_text: Consideration of a motion to adjourn from City Council and convene as the Boulder Municipal Property Authority Board of Directors and;
motions.vote_text: The motion to adjourn from City Council and convene as the Boulder Municipal Property Authority Board of Directors was approved by acclamation.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Riggle moved, seconded by Gray to adopt BMPA Resolution No. 111 formally adopting the 2005 budget for the Boulder Municipal Property Authority.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:0; Schultheiss and Toor absent.

motions.motion_text: Consideration of a motion to adjourn from the Boulder Municipal Property Authority Board of Directors and convene as the Central Area General Improvement District Board of Directors and;
motions.vote_text: The motion to adjourn from the Boulder Municipal Property Authority Board of Directors and convene as the Central Area General Improvement District Board of Directors was approved by acclamation.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember McGrath moved, seconded by Eldridge to adopt CAGID Resolution Nos. 208, 209 and 210.
Consideration of a motion to adjourn from the Central Area General Improvement District Board of Directors and convene as the University Hill General Improvement District Board of Directors and;
motions.vote_text: The motion to adjourn from the Central Area General Improvement District Board of Directors and convene as the University Hill General Improvement District Board of Directors was approved by acclamation.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Stoakes moved, seconded by Eldridge to adopt UHGID Resolution Nos. 148, 149 and 150.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:0; Gray and Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Consideration of a motion to adjourn from the University Hill General Improvement District Board of Directors and convene as the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District Board of Directors and;
motions.vote_text: The motion to adjourn from the University Hill General Improvement District Board of Directors and convene as the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District Board of Directors was approved by acclamation.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember McGrath moved, seconded by Toor to adopt FGGID Resolution Nos. 16, 17 and 18.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:0; Gray and Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Gray moved, seconded by Riggle to suspend the rules and continue the meeting at 10:45p.m.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 7:1; Eldridge opposed, Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: Consideration of a motion to adjourn from the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District Board of Directors and re-convene as City Council.
motions.vote_text: The motion to adjourn from the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District Board of Directors and re-convene as City Council was approved by acclamation.

motions.motion_text: Councilmember Gray moved, seconded by McGrath to continue the Water Rate Structure item to the December 21, 2004 council meeting with a primary focus on WRAB discrepancy and cost estimates.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 6:0; Eldridge, Riggle and Schultheiss absent.

motions.motion_text: There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 11:53 P.M.
motions.vote_text: There being no further business to come before Council at this time, BY MOTION REGULARLY ADOPTED, THE MEETING WAS ADJOURNED AT 11:53 P.M.

agenda_items.section: CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL
agenda_items.title: CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Mayor Ruzzin called the special November 30, 2004 meeting of the Boulder City Council to order at 6:00p.m. in the Council Chambers.

agenda_items.title: PUBLIC HEARINGS
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council held public hearings on the budget and water rate structure, adopted the budget ordinances and resolutions, and continued the water rate structure item.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF THE FOLLOWING ITEMS RELATING TO THE 2005 BUDGET:
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinances Nos. 7403, 7404, 7405 and 7406, rejected the motion to introduce an ordinance rescinding the Trash Tax component, and directed the City Manager to bring back library funding options.

agenda_items.title: PUBLIC HEARING ON THE PROPOSED 2005 CITY OF BOULDER BUDGET; AND
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council held a public hearing on the proposed 2005 City of Boulder budget.

agenda_items.title: SECOND READING AND CONSIDERATION OF ORDINANCE NO. 7403 WHICH ADOPTS A BUDGET FOR THE CITY OF BOULDER, COLORADO, FOR THE FISCAL YEAR COMMENCING ON THE FIRST DAY OF JANUARY, 2005 AND ENDING ON THE LAST DAY OF DECEMBER, 2005, AND SETTING FORTH DETAILS IN RELATION THERETO; AND
agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinance No. 7403.

agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinance No. 7404.

agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinance No. 7406.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF A RESOLUTION FORMALLY ADOPTING THE 2005 BUDGET FOR THE BOULDER MUNICIPAL PROPERTY AUTHORITY.

open_comment_speakers.name: Tim Thomas
open_comment_speakers.topic: Trash Tax – indicated that if the Trash Tax is increased the funds should go to restoring services such as library hours. Stated additional oversight needed for city purchasing.

open_comment_speakers.name: Jann Scott
open_comment_speakers.topic: CATV – spoke of the fundraising efforts currently planned to meet council expectations.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lou Dellacava
open_comment_speakers.topic: (pooled time with Violet Schmidt) representing Boulder Tomorrow – spoke to the numerous problems related to the Trash Tax increase – process, timing, equity, noting that during a time when the Boulder economy continues to decline is not appropriate.

open_comment_speakers.name: Earl McLaughlin
open_comment_speakers.topic: President of Boulder Tomorrow – spoke to the investments of Xcel Energy to bring energy efficiency. Urged council to get better information.

open_comment_speakers.name: Donald Wilson
open_comment_speakers.topic: Trash Tax – indicated that the trash tax is available to the general fund. It is a huge increase and its intended use adds to staffing levels at a time when departments are cutting staff and programs. It sends the wrong message.

open_comment_speakers.name: Gale Dunlap
open_comment_speakers.topic: Trash Tax proposal – blatantly acts as a disincentive to conservation and recycling (see attachment).

open_comment_speakers.name: Jane Jenkins
open_comment_speakers.topic: Representing DBI – requesting that the Trash Tax be tabled until the community has opportunity to discuss and fully understand the issue.

open_comment_speakers.name: Eric Johnson
open_comment_speakers.topic: spoke in support of the tax increase noting that global warming is critical and must be addressed now. Encouraged residents and businesses to reduce waste.

open_comment_speakers.name: Steve Clason
open_comment_speakers.topic: Library Commission Member – spoke to the library funding issue noting that while there is a savings from closing the library early, other negative impacts should be considered including the reduction of meeting space. Asked council to find the $15,000.

open_comment_speakers.name: Alan Streater
open_comment_speakers.topic: supports trash tax – also suggested a head tax. Thanks for clearing bike paths.

open_comment_speakers.name: Todd Runestad
open_comment_speakers.topic: Trash Tax – feels this is mission creep – original purpose not being maintained. Wrong time for a tax increase – felt it should be placed on a ballot.

open_comment_speakers.name: Inta Morris
open_comment_speakers.topic: Rocky Mountain Climate Organization – speaking to the effects of climate change in Boulder. Less snow pack and less water will create major drought conditions. Emphasis on renewables and energy efficiencies needs to remain a priority.

open_comment_speakers.name: Steve Pomerance
open_comment_speakers.topic: supports energy efficiencies but does not feel this proposal is the right way to address that project. Concerned that far more over sight is needed.

open_comment_speakers.name: Leslie Glustrom
open_comment_speakers.topic: spoke to the importance of addressing green house gas emissions.

open_comment_speakers.name: Dan Powers
open_comment_speakers.topic: Chamber of Commerce – requested that the Trash Tax increase be removed form consideration this evening to allow Business community to analyze the impacts.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lisa Dilling
open_comment_speakers.topic: Scientist – in support of utilizing Trash Tax funds to address a critical problem.

open_comment_speakers.name: Pam Milmoe
open_comment_speakers.topic: in support of utilizing the trash tax to benefit the environment. Leadership in this area is critical.

open_comment_speakers.name: Francoise Poinsatte
open_comment_speakers.topic: noted that when Boulder adopted the resolution in support of the Kyoto Protocol it was clear that addressing energy conservation would be key.

open_comment_speakers.name: Ken Regelson
open_comment_speakers.topic: Let's start acting locally – pass the Trash Tax.

open_comment_speakers.name: Guy Errickson
open_comment_speakers.topic: supports public access TV, but noted that current program doesn't meet that definition.

open_comment_speakers.name: Alison Burchell
open_comment_speakers.topic: re: trash tax - spoke to the importance of engaging in community dialogue. Indicated support of the program, but better outreach needed.

open_comment_speakers.name: Bruce Bland
open_comment_speakers.topic: Urged support of the Trash Tax – echoed that better communication needed, but felt it important to take this important step to address a critical problem.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lisa Morzel
open_comment_speakers.topic: spoke to the importance of supporting the Trash Tax, noting that consumers have a choice – if they reduce waste the cost can be less. Encouraged approval.

open_comment_speakers.name: Donna Marek
open_comment_speakers.topic: re: Channel 54 – indicated that the contract between the city and CATV is not valid. Indicated that mismanagement is evident and urged council to remove funding for CATV from the 2005 budget.

open_comment_speakers.name: Dan Powers
open_comment_speakers.topic: supported staff alternative “Tailored.”

open_comment_speakers.name: Peter Mayer
open_comment_speakers.topic: supported WRAB Water Budget proposal.

open_comment_speakers.name: Jim Knoff
open_comment_speakers.topic: voiced his support for the water budget approach.

open_comment_speakers.name: Michael Brawner
open_comment_speakers.topic: supported classic water budget proposal by WRAB.

open_comment_speakers.name: Bill Deoro
open_comment_speakers.topic: spoke in support of the WRAB Water Budget proposal.

open_comment_speakers.name: Charles Bergren
open_comment_speakers.topic: representing Gunbarrel Homeowner’s Association; they purchase water (2 million gallons) to water neighborhood park – supports WRAB “classic” approach.

open_comment_speakers.name: Eric Johnson
open_comment_speakers.topic: supports “classic” WRAB water budget proposal.

open_comment_speakers.name: Steve Pomerance
open_comment_speakers.topic: supports water budget approach but indicated that pricing rate structure still needs to be addressed.

open_comment_speakers.name: Amy Livingston
open_comment_speakers.topic: urged council to support the “classic” water budget approach proposed by the WRAB.

open_comment_speakers.name: Francoise Poinsatte
open_comment_speakers.topic: provided some background from when she was on council. Indicated support for the classic water budget approach.

open_comment_speakers.name: Hampton Islan
open_comment_speakers.topic: favors the budget rate structure.

open_comment_speakers.name: Elise Jones
open_comment_speakers.topic: spoke in support of the WRAB proposal for classic water budget approach.
